text:
sasha: quickstart blocked me for ~30m. local curl to /v1/generate -> 200, but our sample using the Ruby SDK returns 402 PaymentRequired. Console shows billing active. Anyone?
onboarding-bot: Workspace 'spark-sandbox' provisioned. Note: attach billing to workspace if required by org policy.
morgan: Paste the minimal repro and the exact token you used (redact ok). Also are you using a personal key or a service account?
sasha: running the sample in GH Actions. The workflow injects `secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Locally I used my personal key — works. In CI the logs show `Authorization: Bearer ` (blank) but SDK still makes a call and then hits 402.
sdk-bot: Tip: SDKs should fail fast if token is empty. Returning 402 from the gateway in that flow is confusing.
morgan: Two possibilities: (1) empty key -> gateway treating request as anonymous and mapping to a workspace bucket that needs billing, or (2) token present but scoped to embeddings-only (service token) which can't call /generate. That would also return a 402-ish billing error in some routing configs.
sasha: Ah! Our org's CI uses a short-lived service token minted by the infra team for embedding ingestion. It was accidentally used in the quickstart workflow. The token has scope:embeddings only.
morgan: That explains it. Gateway rejects non-embedding attempts with a Billing/Authorization mix error when scope mismatch occurs for paid endpoints. SDK retry loop made it worse because it retried on 5xx but not on auth scope mismatch.
sasha: Workaround: swapped the CI secret to a full workspace key for the smoke job and the Ruby sample call succeeded.
ci-bot: Note: GitHub Actions for forks won't have secrets; maintainers must run workflows or use a mock path.
docs: Action items I can take: add a quick FAQ blurb "402 on generate in CI" explaining: check secret presence, ensure key scope includes generative endpoints, prefer workspace-scoped service tokens for CI, and how to verify token scopes via `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami`.
sdk-bot: Filed issue RED-9804: "SDKs: detect empty/mis-scoped keys at startup; surface clear error: \"Missing/invalid API key or insufficient scope: set REDWOOD_API_KEY with workspace or full-scope service key.\" Also avoid retrying on auth/scope errors"
morgan: I will update the sample CI: (1) add a check-secrets step that fails with a clear message when the key is missing, (2) add a smoke/mock path for untrusted PRs, (3) add a small note in README about token scopes. PR: https://github.com/redwood/sample-app/pull/777
sasha: Also logged the debugging snippet inside the sample: `# check token scope
res = curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami
echo $res` so CI can early-fail with a helpful message.
docs: I'll add the whoami snippet and an explanation of common scope names (embeddings, generate, admin).
sasha: First successful sample run after swapping to workspace-scoped key. Leaving thread for the onboarding guide. :white_check_mark:
